description: The bar chart illustrates the percentage of biased responses generated by language models before and after instruction tuning, categorized by three types of contact: Support of Authorities, Extended Contact, and Virtual Contact. Each category contains four bars representing different conditions: "No Contact Before" (light gray), "Positive Contact Before" (light red), "Negative Contact Before" (light blue), and their corresponding "After" conditions (darker shades: dark gray, dark red, dark blue). The y-axis represents "Bias Percentage," ranging from 0 to 70, with values labeled on top of each bar. For "Support of Authorities," the bias percentages before tuning are 39.50%, 31.83%, and 42.38% for the three contact types, while after tuning, they drop to 0.04%, 0.00%, and 0.00%, respectively. Similarly, for "Extended Contact," the bias percentages decrease from 40.61%, 36.13%, and 47.28% to 0.00%, 0.00%, and 0.11%. In the "Virtual Contact" category, bias percentages before tuning are 39.74%, 39.17%, and 43.83%, and after tuning, they are 10.00%, 10.01%, and 10.02%. The chart shows that instruction tuning significantly reduces bias across all categories, especially for Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, where bias is reduced to nearly zero, while a notable residual bias remains in Virtual Contact. The darker shaded bars (after tuning) are positioned on top of the lighter shaded bars (before tuning), visually indicating the reduction in bias.
